details:
HERO: Human Exploration Readiness & Ocular Assistant

Stepping Beyond Our Comfort Zone

Stepping beyond our comfort zone is never easy. Every step brings new problems, new adjustments and new challenges. For astronauts on long-duration deep space missions, those challenges are severe and connected to one another. Microgravity can trigger Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), a leading risk to crew vision and performance. Isolation wears down mental resilience. And on a Mars-class mission, a message to Earth can take up to about 22 minutes each way, so real-time medical guidance is often out of reach.

Yet ambition and vision keep us moving forward. NASA’s vision is to explore the secrets of the universe for the benefit of all. That vision is what carries crews into the dark.

But vision alone cannot carry anyone across it. What keeps people going is support: someone who notices, who understands, and who helps us take the next step with confidence. That is where HERO comes in.

Meet HERO

HERO is an AI-driven crew health monitoring platform and hands-free voice companion. It works as an autonomous co-pilot. It brings together ocular telemetry, vital signs and cabin environmental data to assess mental and cognitive readiness in real time. It then explains what it finds in clear, calm, human language.

What HERO Does

  • One view, three data streams (7 × 7 × 7). Seven ocular OCT variables (our primary focus, SANS), seven mental health and performance variables (such as heart rate variability, sleep, vocal latency, reaction time and affect), and seven ISS cabin variables (CO₂, radiation, noise, VOCs, thermal comfort, light/circadian cues and water quality). That is 21 variables per astronaut per mission day.
  • Readiness scoring. SANS risk, mental load and cabin risk are combined into one overall readiness score.
  • Early risk flagging. Risk is calculated from the astronaut’s own record, including sub-clinical levels, so concerning patterns can be noticed before they become critical.
  • Ocular digital twin. An interactive 3D eye (fundus map, sagittal section, whole globe) with layers for RNFL quadrants, macular GCIPL and choroidal folds. Findings can be located, not just listed.
  • HERO voice co-pilot. Say “Hi HERO” and ask by voice or text, in English or Indonesian. HERO explains which variables are out of range and why.
  • What-if protocols. Switch countermeasures (LBNP, cabin adjustments, behavioral health support) on and off and watch the scores respond.
  • Sensor-ready by design. Today the prototype receives simulated data through an input simulator. HERO is built as an intermediate layer that can later receive real sensor feeds.

How It Works

  1. Collect: crew records per astronaut per mission day.
  2. Analyze: scoring engine and machine learning models turn raw values into risk and readiness.
  3. Explain & Act: dashboard, digital twin and voice translate complex biomarkers into clear clinical insight, protocols can be tried instantly to see their effect.

Why It Matters

  • Autonomy: gives crews meaningful insight when Earth cannot answer in time.
  • Clarity: turns cross-system biomarkers into actionable understanding.
  • Integration: eyes, mind and environment in one place instead of separate tools.
  • Comfort: hands-free and low-strain, suited to microgravity tasks and vision-related symptoms.
  • Companionship: a familiar voice for a very unfamiliar place.

Intended Impact

HERO supports the exploration journey itself. By keeping crews healthy and mission-ready, it helps the mission continue. The same approach could also help on Earth, in remote clinics, polar stations and other isolated settings where specialist care is far away.

Under the Hood

  • Front end: React 18, Tailwind CSS, Lucide icons, Geist typeface.
  • Digital twin: custom WebGL rendering.
    • cabin environment: greenhouse sensor data (temperature, humidity, illumination);
    • mental health and performance: HRV features such as MEAN_RR, RMSSD, SDNN, HR and pNN25;
    • ocular: a glaucoma clinical dataset (10,000 records).
  • Deployment: Vercel. Hardware: only a laptop with a browser and microphone.

Model Evaluation (held-out test data)

  • Mental health model (HRV, Normal vs Stress): 73,858 test samples, 100% accuracy, ROC-AUC 1.00.
  • Cabin environment model: 3,432 test samples, 100% accuracy, ROC-AUC 1.00.
  • Ocular model (glaucoma risk, Age/IOP/CDR/pachymetry): 48.95% accuracy on 2,000 held-out samples, which is at chance level. The dataset shows no learnable signal for these features, so this model is an experimental pipeline placeholder, not a clinical predictor. HERO’s SANS risk comes from its OCT-based scoring engine, and we plan to retrain this model on real OCT data (RNFL, GCC) with clinician-confirmed labels.

We read the perfect scores as a sign that these labeled datasets are cleanly separable, not as proof of real-world performance. The glaucoma result is close to chance, so we treat that model as experimental while we look for stronger data. We state this openly because crew-safety tools must earn trust.

What Makes HERO Creative

  • Combines eye health, mental health and cabin environment, usually studied separately, into one view.
  • Pairs a clinical digital twin with a conversational voice companion.
  • Bilingual, hands-free, and designed around the real delay in communicating with Earth.

What We Considered

  • Communication delay and the need for crew autonomy.
  • The isolation and strangeness of space, which led us to build a companion, not only a monitor.
  • Low-strain design (dark interface, voice-first) for crews with vision changes.
  • Explainability: every score can be explained in plain language.
  • Privacy: records stay on the user’s device.
  • Scalability: ready for real sensors and further models.
  • Safety: HERO supports decisions and does not replace medical judgment.

Limits and What’s Next

HERO currently runs on simulated data, and our datasets are terrestrial proxies rather than astronaut data. Next, we will connect real sensor feeds, validate the models on spaceflight-relevant data, integrate the cabin and mental models into the scoring, and add trend forecasting.

Our Hope

The universe will keep its secrets for a long time, and those who go looking for them will often meet the unknown far from home. We hope HERO is there in those moments: a steady voice that stays calm when everything else feels uncertain, and that sees the person behind every reading, never just a number on a screen.

We hope it gives crews insight they can trust: clear, grounded in their own data, and honest about what it knows and what it does not, so that every decision stays in their hands, even when Earth is minutes away.

And we hope that wherever the mission leads, they return safe, strong and ready for the next one.

“You don’t have to be a Superhuman to be a HERO.”

HERO is here so every astronaut can take that next step, and keep exploring.
